newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Pioneer International chief executive John Schubert said yesterday the company is considering selling its A$600 million share in Australia's largest petroleum refiner and marketer, Australian Petroleum Ltd, because of weak returns. Merchant banks J.P.Morgan and Macquarie Bank have been hired to assist with a strategic review of the business. Page 1.

Commercial property has been off to a strong start in Australia for 1997, with the A$82 million purchase by Colonial Commercial Property Trust of the former Capita complex in Perth, the sale of the giant Coles site in Brisbane, the 25 percent profit in Melbourne by one recession buyer, and the line up of players for the New South Wales government's A$120 million-plus Pacific Power tower. Page 1.

Red-faced Treasury officials will embark on a major probe of 200 companies in an attempt to explain the A$1.6 billion corporate tax shortfall. Speaking at a Senate economic committee yesterday, officials attributed part of the shortfall to companies revaluing stocks to take advantage of the 1995 rise in the corporate tax rate. The committee also revealed at least 170 errors in the mid-year budget review released in January, which included a A$1.2 billion error in the estimate of the general government undelying deficit for 1996/97. Page 3.

The Howard Government has come under increasing pressure to reject a draft report from the Productivity Commission which recommends car tariffs be slashed to five percent by 2004. Many of the government's ministers as well as several state premiers have expressed caution towards the report, fearing its recommendations could destroy the car industry in Victoria and South Australia. The Labor Party has reversed its stance on the issue which dominated party-policy in the 1980s, announcing it supports a freeze in the levels of automotive tariffs until 2005. Page 4.

Pioneer International Ltd chief executive John Schubert said yesterday the group will attempt to offset its exposure to the weak Australian markets and try to boost its full-year earnings past the A$300 million mark by expanding its United States and Asian operations. Pioneer may build a million-tonne cement plant in Texas, which could cost over A$100 million, and is looking at new businesses in the U.S. sunbelt region and in eastern China. Page 17.

WMC Ltd is now A$240 million ahead of its expectations for its entire oil portfolio after selling its oil assets last year. Novus Petroleum Ltd yesterday paid A$183 million for a 30 percent stake of the East Spar gas field and associated exploration acreageoff the West Australian coast. WMC has now received A$588 million for its petroleum assets. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Pioneer International yesterday announced it is considering selling its 50 percent stake in the retail petrol industry leader Ampol. After announcing another dismal profit performance, Pioneer said weak performances from its Ampol investment attributed to its profit drop of 16 percent to A$112.7 million. Page 23.

Network Ten has re-signed key programming source Columbia Tri-Star, which produces top-rating shows The Nanny and Seinfeld, until 2000. The deal includes Columbia producing films and TV drama in Australia for the first time. Ten was able to fight off rival Seven Network for the signing. Page 23.

Australian Stock Exchange managing director Dick Humphrey said yesterday the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial systems could be the last chance to achieve the reforms needed to position Australia as a regional financial centre. Humphrey said inqury head Stan Wallis needs to ignore his terms of reference and recommend tax changes that would increase Australia's competitiveness. Page 23.

Ford Australia yesterday announced a record after-tax profit of A$217.3 million for the 1996 calendar year, 7.7 per cent higher than 1995. The result is due largely to successful sales of Ford's Falcon and a buoyant Australian dollar. President David Morgan said the company was able to achieve the figures despite intense import competition. Page 23.

Chevron Corp's Dionysys-1 well off the West Australian coast, which was drilled in the middle of 1996, has found a major gas reservoir close to the Chrysaor and Gorgon gas fields. The find, the announcement of which was delayed because a nearby exploration block was up for tender, will significantly expand Chevron's gas reserves. Page 25.

Base metals producer Pasminco Ltd yesterday announced a A$20.2 million net profit for the half year to December 31, surprising the market after unfavourable conditions over the reporting period that saw profits forecast at between A$5 and A$15 million. Pasminco managing director David Stewart was happy with the result after a high dollar and low zinc prices threatened profit. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Pioneer International managing director John Schubert and investment banks JP Morgan and Macquarie will reassess Pioneer's A$561 involvement with struggling petrol refining and retailing group Ampol after Pioneer revealed a 16 percent fall in December profit to A$112 million yesterday. Schubert declined to comment on specific options for the sale of the 50 percent stake. However, one option would be for Caltex, which owns the remaining half of Ampol, to acquire the interest. Page 27.

GIO may transform its highly lucrative reinsurance business, now one of the company's best performers, into a separate company after roaring share prices in recent weeks. Stockbrokers and merchant bankers have been lobbying hard in recent weeks to separate the reinsurance arm, arguing it is the best way to generate healthy returns to GIO shareholders. It is expected that around 80 percent of the business profit will come from reinsurance this year. Page 27.

Caltex Australia has announced a 10 percent increase in annual net profits to A$47.2 million from the year to December from A$42.6 the previous year. The increase has been fuelled by savings of around $A44 million from its merger with Ampol. The news was well received by the market which pushed Caltex shares up 13 cents to close at A$4.40, further helped by positive comments about the company by Australian Petroleum chief executive Ian Blackburne. Page 27.

Stadium Australia is looking to increase the sales of its gold and platinum packages in a bid to raise A$365 million after revelations the four investment banks who had unconditionally guaranteed the A$365 million public float to build Sydney's Olympic stadium at Homebush are understood to have a collective exposure of about A$240 million to the project. Page 27.

The Howard Government is in desperate negotiations with the Opposition and minor parties in an attempt to pass amendments to the telecommunications bill before it is debated in the Senate. Communications Minister Richard Alston was last night finaliing talks with his counterpart Chris Schacht, with the focal point being an improved competitive environment for new entrants and service providers. If the government cannot not finalise a deal with the Opposition before March 18 there remains little chance of the bill being passed before July 1 when the telecommunications industry is due to be regulated. Page 27.

Aridane Australia Ltd has announced a A$18.6 million profit for the December half, helped by a A$16 million abnormal provision relating to the sale of a business in 1982 which it was awarded costs. The interim result compares favourably with $A2.7 million last year and comes at a time the company is looking at a major development complex on a Brisbane CBD property. Page 31.
THE AGE

Following its 16 percent fall in December half-year profit to A$112.7 million, Pioneer International managing director John Schubert said the company was re-evaluating its A$561 million investment in struggling petrol refining and retailing group Ampol in order to focus on global expansion in the building materials industry. Page B1.

Caltex Australia posted a 10 percent increase in annual net profits with figures for the 12 months to December of A$47.2 million up from A$42.6 million the previous year. The company has defeated tough conditions in the petrol refining industry to post the profit which was driven by cost savings from its merger with Ampol. Page B1.

Amid controversy over the status of the casino management contract at Perth's Burswood Hotel, Japanese-based company Victoria Co group yesterday sold its stake in Burswood Property Trust, the owner of the Perth casino, for A$30 million. The West Australin Gaming Commission is yet to receive any documentation relating to the proposed sale and transfer of the casino management contract unveiled by Victoria in December. Page B1.

Ford Australia has announced a record profit of $A217.3 million for the 1996 calendar year which was A$15.6 million better than the company's previous record in 1985. The results come only a day after Ford Australia president David Morgan warned the company might quit Australia after the Productivity Commission report was released, recommending car tariffs be slashed to just five percent by 2004. Ford attributed the good showing on its A$1 billion investment programme and strong sales of its new vehicles. Page B3.

The Supreme Court has heard that the Seven network never seriously considered an offer by the pay TV operator Foxtel before signing a joint venture with its rival Optus Vision in 1995. Seven's deputy chairman Peter Ritchie said that at no stage did his company seriously consider Foxtel's offer, and later likened Foxtel to a "stalking horse" to use against Optus Vision in negotiations. Page B2.

Ansett has announced plans for a new plane-sharing agreement with Air New Zealand only days after the Kiwi airline scrapped similar arrangements with its 20 percent shareholder Qantas. Under the deal, the airlines will sell tickets under their own names but use one another's flights, enabling them to exploit brand names without the cost of putting on actual flights. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
